label: LEGITIMATE_INDEPENDENT_CHANGE
rationale: The commit (chore: remplace la formule de la retraite de base par celle de l'Urssaf) replaces, for artisans/commerçants/PLNR, the two-tranche formula (17,15 % of the base within the PSS + 0,60/0,72 % of the whole base) by a barème taking 17,75/17,87 % up to the PSS and 0,60/0,72 % above it, moves the CNAVPL two-tranche rule to `profession libérale . CNAVPL . retraite de base`, and changes the denominator of `protection sociale . retraite . base . revenu cotisé` from 17,15 % to taux T1. With respect to the only bounded article involved, D633-3 LEGIARTI000049904636 (periods from 2025-01-01), the new barème is algebraically the same amount: (17,15+0,72) % x min(A,PSS) + 0,72 % x max(A-PSS,0) = 17,15 % x min(A,PSS) + 0,72 % x A; the engine confirms it: identical `retraite de base` in 73 of 81 checks and a 1 € rounding difference in 8 (single rounding after vs rounding of each tranche before; D633-3 fixes no rounding). So it is not a mismatch; it is also not harmless, because what the engine computes did change: the published rate `taux T1` is now 17,87 % instead of the text's 17,15 % (0,72 % folded in, Urssaf presentation), and the derived `revenu cotisé`, `trimestres` and pension estimate change for every non-CNAVPL case below the PSS (e.g. revenu cotisé 20 700 -> 20 000 €/an, trimestres 4 -> 3 at 6 800 €/an in 2024, 3 -> 2 at the minimum base in 2025). Those derived rules rest on R351-9, R634-1, D634-1, D633-2 and L161-17-3, and the CNAVPL branch on D642-3/D642-4: all outside the bounded set, so I cannot adjudicate them. The commit itself says the method was adopted at the Urssaf's insistence (outside source). Pre-2025 rates (17,75 / 0,60 %) cannot be checked: D633-3 LEGIARTI000041967101 has no text in S9 (abstain).
